read.where: The **programs** in this book carry the knowledge: Level 1 for everyone, Level 2 for bartenders, Level 3 for the craft. On the bar, a new bartender **shadows** a strong one, then builds drinks while you **watch**. Sign off a practical only after you’ve **seen** it done to spec.
read.mixup: Passing a quiz isn’t the same as making the drink. The **practical** is where you see it.

one drink or one standard tonight.

read.bigIdea: Ten minutes that set the night.
read.where: Pre-shift is short and the same every night: what’s **86’d** and what to offer instead, tonight’s **focus** (one drink or one standard), anything new on the menu, and a quick **check** (the book’s Quick Quiz works). Pin the notes in **Team Chat** so the late arrival reads them too.
read.mixup: Pre-shift isn’t a lecture. **One** focus sticks; ten don’t.
read.sayIt: We’re out of the lavender syrup tonight, but I can make it with honey instead.

read.where: A guest should get the **same drink** from any bartender on any night. That means every pour is **measured** with a jigger, every drink follows the **spec**, the **glass**, the **ice** and the **garnish**. When you see a drift, fix it **on the spot**, quietly and kindly, and change the spec only through you.
read.mixup: A “good” free pour isn’t a standard. A **jigger** is.

keyPoints.line: no one on staff may be intoxicated at work.
the GM before any tasting with alcohol.
taste: a sip, not a drink.

read.bigIdea: Taste to learn, never to drink.
read.where: Tasting is how a team learns a menu, but it has limits. Michigan’s Liquor Control Code says a licensee’s **employees may not be intoxicated** on the premises. So any tasting that involves alcohol happens only under **our license and HR policy**, set by the **GM**. Tasting **syrups**, **citrus** and spec checks with a **straw** (Level 3) is part of the job.

stops.name: Learn
stops.text: Talk about **balance** and the selling line.

read.mixup: A staff tasting isn’t a staff drink. It’s a **sip** to learn from.
